after.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS
verificationCriteria: When a live preview session is active, the page displays the draft content of the requested entry — for example, a field value that has been saved as a draft but not yet published.
When a draft entry field is modified during an active live preview session, the updated field value appears on the page without a full page reload.
When no live preview session is active, the page displays the published content for each entry.
When the page is accessed with a live preview session active, the page loads and renders the entry content successfully.

notes: This is a novel feature — the codebase has zero live_preview/livePreview references. The Contentstack SDK initialization in src/services/contentstack.ts (the `options` object fed to `contentstack.Stack()`) is the primary attachment point: the vendor docs require a live_preview config block on Stack initialization. The app entry point src/pages/_app.tsx is where the Live Preview SDK init call would be wired. The ContentstackContext/useContent hook is the data flow that must be updated when draft content changes arrive. Note: the project uses Next.js Pages Router (src/pages/_app.tsx), not App Router, so the vendor's App Router guide must be adapted. Part of the setup (custom preview URL configuration in the Contentstack dashboard) is a vendor-console task, not code — it is a prerequisite but not verifiable in this suite.

notes: Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array with useful architectural notes. I built the full AC list from scratch based on codebase inspection. Key findings from reading the actual files: (1) src/services/contentstack.ts exports `options: contentstack.Config` and `Stack = contentstack.Stack(options)` — the `options` object currently has no `live_preview` block, confirming it is the primary attachment point. (2) src/pages/_app.tsx uses Pages Router with no Contentstack Live Preview SDK init — the vendor's App Router guide must be adapted. (3) src/hooks/useContent.ts reads from `ContentstackContext` via useContext and exposes `getContentByKey` — this is the data-flow path that must surface draft content to components. (4) Zero `live_preview`/`livePreview` references exist anywhere in the codebase. (5) The ContentstackFactory class wraps Stack and is used by getEntry, getSingleEntry, findSingletonEntry, getInteractiveMapsStackEntry — all must support draft content delivery (AC-10). (6) The story's noted limitation about protected pages is captured in AC-7. (7) AC-14 addresses bundle-size concern since live preview is client-only. The ContentstackContext file was not found by search — it may be auto-generated, in a different path, or not yet created; this does not affect the ACs since they describe observable outcomes regardless of file location.
